# Aunt Jamesina

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v3 ch.Relationships P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052), [v3 ch.Interlude P6](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0006)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Aunt Jimsie  <sub>[v3 ch.Friend P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 ch.Relationships P47](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0047), [v3 ch.Charming P1](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0001), [v3 ch.Gardners’Call P0](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0000)</sub>; Aunty J.  <sub>[v3 ch.Jonas P5](../source/v03-c24.md#nw-v03-c24-p0005)</sub>

## Appearance

Aunt Jamesina is a tiny old woman featuring a softly-triangular face with pink cheeks and large, soft blue eyes. She wears her snow-white hair styled in quaint little puffs over her ears.

_Sources: [v3 ch.Relationships P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052)_

## Personality

Aunt Jamesina is a sweet and old-fashioned woman who retains a youthful spirit, considering herself to never have outgrown her teens. Mirthful in disposition, she holds a proper respect for the clergy, though she dislikes visiting others because of the trouble it entails.

_Sources: [v3 ch.Friend P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 ch.Relationships P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053), [v3 ch.Anne-girl P2](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0002), [v3 ch.Interlude P1](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0001), [v3 ch.Speaks P10](../source/v03-c20.md#nw-v03-c20-p0010), [v3 ch.B.A.’s P42](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0042)_

## History

Aunt Jamesina was named after her father, James, who drowned at sea a month before her birth. She was given a pet cat, the Sarah-cat, by her washerwoman. She arrived at Patty's Place with her cats, [Joseph](../character/joseph.md) and the Sarah-cat, to serve as a chaperone for [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md), [Stella Maynard](../character/stella-maynard.md), [Priscilla](../character/priscilla-grant.md), and [Philippa Gordon](../character/phil-gordon.md). During her time keeping house with the college girls, she offered them her relaxed philosophy on chaperoning and joined in discussions regarding household expenses, beauty, marriage, and potential suitors. At the conclusion of their final examinations, Aunt Jamesina gathered with the girls to reflect on what their four years at [Redmond College](../codex/places.md#redmond-college) had taught them before they packed up Patty's Place at the end of their studies.

_Sources: [v3 ch.Friend P3](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0003), [v3 ch.Friend P6](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0006), [v3 ch.Friend P7](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0007), [v3 ch.Friend P8](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0008), [v3 ch.Friend P10](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0010), [v3 ch.Friend P11](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0011), +341 more_

## Quotes

> "She couldn’t take Joseph with her so she begged me to take him. I really couldn’t refuse. He’s a beautiful cat—that is, his disposition is beautiful. She called him Joseph because his coat is of many colors."
>
> — Aunt Jamesina — [v3 ch.Relationships P56](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0056)

> "Kittens have to be drowned, I admit, or the world would be overrun. But no decent, grown-up cat should be done to death—unless he sucks eggs."
>
> — Aunt Jamesina — [v3 ch.Relationships P69](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0069)

> “I suppose you feel kind of, sorry” said Aunt Jamesina. “The teens are such a nice part of life. I’m glad I’ve never gone out of them myself.”
>
> — Aunt Jamesina — [v3 ch.Interlude P1](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0001)

> "Well, I hope so, Anne. I do hope so, because I love her. But I can’t understand her—she beats me. She isn’t like any of the girls I ever knew, or any of the girls I was myself."
>
> — Aunt Jamesina — [v3 ch.Interlude P40](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0040)

> "Yes, in my soul. But I’ll admit my legs aren’t as young as yours. You go and get some fresh air, Anne. You look pale lately."
>
> — Aunt Jamesina — [v3 ch.Charming P4](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0004)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--aunt-jamesina.md)

Aunt Jamesina acts as a housekeeper and affectionate chaperone for [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) at Patty's Place during Anne's college years. The two share a warm, cozy home life, frequently discussing household duties, past mishaps, and personal milestones like Anne's twentieth birthday. Aunt Jamesina offers [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) a relaxed approach to chaperoning and lighthearted advice on romance and beauty.

- Friend of — housemates and affectionate companions  <sub>[v3 ch.Interlude P0](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0000)</sub>

### [Phil Gordon](../character/phil-gordon.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/aunt-jamesina--phil-gordon.md)

Aunt Jamesina serves as a loving guardian figure to [Phil Gordon](../character/phil-gordon.md) while living together at Patty's Place. She helps manage the household expenses alongside [Phil](../character/phil-gordon.md) and frequently chats with her about suitors, beauty, and marriage. Though Aunt Jamesina appreciates Phil's charming nature, she also reflects privately on the young woman's eccentric personality.

- Friend of — affectionate guardian or mentor figure who loves her  <sub>[v3 ch.Interlude P40](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0040), [v3 ch.Jonas P5](../source/v03-c24.md#nw-v03-c24-p0005)</sub>

### [Priscilla Grant](../character/priscilla-grant.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/aunt-jamesina--priscilla-grant.md)

Aunt Jamesina acts as the chaperone and housekeeper for [Priscilla Grant](../character/priscilla-grant.md) and the other girls living at Patty's Place. [Priscilla](../character/priscilla-grant.md) warmly welcomed Aunt Jamesina into the home for their sophomore year at [Redmond College](../codex/places.md#redmond-college). They maintain an affectionate dynamic as housemates, sharing casual conversation and quiet moments together over their years living under the same roof.

- Friend of — housemates who admired and welcomed her warmly  <sub>[v3 ch.Relationships P51](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0051)</sub>
